gaps.sentence: She ___ her breath before diving into the pool.
gaps.explanation: 'Hold one's breath' — catching breath is recovering it afterwards.

gaps.sentence: He ___ her a compliment on her new hairstyle.
gaps.explanation: pay somebody a compliment is the fixed collocation for praising someone.

gaps.sentence: It took her years to ___ a living from her painting.
gaps.explanation: make a living means to earn enough money to live on.

gaps.sentence: She was bitterly ___ when her proposal was rejected.
gaps.hint: adjective collocating with 'bitterly' after bad news
gaps.explanation: bitterly disappointed is the standard collocation; 'bitterly' combines with negative feelings.

gaps.sentence: Her company ___ a huge profit last year.
gaps.explanation: make a profit (or make a loss) is the fixed business collocation.

gaps.sentence: She ___ attention to every detail of the contract.
He didn't ___ any interest in politics until university.
gaps.explanation: take an interest in something means to become curious or involved in it.

gaps.sentence: The company has ___ enormous losses this quarter.
gaps.explanation: 'Suffer losses' is the standard collocation for experiencing financial loss.
